Issues.Title: Respect reduced motion for indeterminate progress
Issues.Body:
This is a bugfix.

### Proposed solution

Disable the infinite indeterminate progress animation when the user
requests prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. Center the existing background
gradient so the indeterminate indicator remains visible.

The native progress element retains its indeterminate semantics. This
does not turn it into a determinate percentage or hide the indicator.

### Tradeoffs

Users requesting reduced motion see a static indicator. The normal
animation, determinate progress, colors and sizes are unchanged.

### Testing Done

Compile test/dart-sass/regressions/progress-reduced-motion.scss.
Check that @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) contains
.bulma-progress:indeterminate with animation: none and
background-position: center. Compile bulma.scss to verify the full build.

Validated locally with Dart Sass 1.105.2 against upstream main at
c5cd04baf0258cfcc77b4e8610488a0d439effa2. No generated CSS is included.

### Changelog updated?

No. This is a focused source-only bugfix with a regression fixture.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Respect reduced motion for indeterminate progress" (#4068)

Issues.Title: Apply the class prefix to the Grid auto-fill modifier
Issues.Body:
This is a bugfix.

### Proposed solution

The Grid auto-fill modifier is emitted as .is-auto-fill even when
$class-prefix is configured. Other Grid modifiers consistently interpolate
iv.$class-prefix.

Apply the same interpolation to is-auto-fill. With $class-prefix: "bulma-",
the expected selector is .bulma-grid.bulma-is-auto-fill, not
.bulma-grid.is-auto-fill.

### Tradeoffs

The default (empty prefix) output does not change. Consumers that worked
around this bug by using an unprefixed modifier alongside a prefixed Grid
should switch to the consistently prefixed modifier.

### Testing Done

Compile test/dart-sass/regressions/prefixed-grid-auto-fill.scss.
Check that the CSS contains .bulma-grid.bulma-is-auto-fill and does not
contain .bulma-grid.is-auto-fill. Compile bulma.scss and check that the
default selector remains .grid.is-auto-fill.

Validated locally with Dart Sass 1.105.2 against upstream main at
c5cd04baf0258cfcc77b4e8610488a0d439effa2. No generated CSS is included.

### Changelog updated?

No. This is a focused source-only bugfix with a regression fixture.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Apply the class prefix to the Grid auto-fill modifier" (#4067)

Issues.Title: Respect the lightness argument in bulmaFindLightColor
Issues.Body:
This is a bugfix.

### Proposed solution

bulmaFindLightColor($color, $l: 96%) currently resets $l to 96% immediately,
so callers cannot use the existing optional argument.

Remove that reset and compare the input lightness against the requested
value rather than a hard-coded 96%. Keep already-lighter inputs unchanged.
The default call remains unchanged.

Example: bulmaFindLightColor(#336699, 90%) should have 90% HSL lightness,
not 96%. A 98%-light input should stay at 98%.

### Tradeoffs

Callers that pass an explicit lightness now get the requested behavior.
The default, function signature, invalid-input behavior and color space
handling are otherwise unchanged.

### Testing Done

Compile test/dart-sass/regressions/light-color-parameter.scss with Dart Sass.
The fixture raises @error for an incorrect custom value, default value or
already-lighter input. Compile bulma.scss to verify the full build.

Validated locally with Dart Sass 1.105.2 against upstream main at
c5cd04baf0258cfcc77b4e8610488a0d439effa2. No generated CSS is included.

### Changelog updated?

No. This is a focused source-only bugfix with a regression fixture.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Respect the lightness argument in bulmaFindLightColor" (#4066)

Issues.Title: Fix sRGB transfer function in relative luminance
Issues.Body:
This is a bugfix.

### Proposed solution

Use the sRGB transfer function specified by WCAG relative luminance:
the linear branch at or below 0.04045, and exponent 2.4 in the nonlinear
branch. The current implementation uses exponent 2 and threshold 0.03928.

For example, bulmaColorLuminance(#777) currently returns approximately
0.2445013464, rather than the reference value 0.184474994500441.

Remove an unused local variable. Preserve the existing invalid-input
fallback and the separate inverse-color policy.

Reference: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/relative-luminance.html

### Tradeoffs

This changes derived luminance values and may alter colors that depend on
them. It does not change the public API, the inverse-color threshold, or
the contrast helper's existing policy. A contrast-policy redesign should
be discussed separately.

### Testing Done

Compile test/dart-sass/regressions/srgb-luminance.scss with Dart Sass.
The fixture raises @error for incorrect black, white, middle gray and
values near the sRGB breakpoint. Compile bulma.scss to verify the full build.

Validated locally with Dart Sass 1.105.2 against upstream main at
c5cd04baf0258cfcc77b4e8610488a0d439effa2. No generated CSS is included.

### Changelog updated?

No. This is a focused source-only bugfix with a regression fixture.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Fix sRGB transfer function in relative luminance" (#4065)

Issues.Title: `.menu-list` uses physical `text-align: left`, breaking menu alignment under dir="rtl"
Issues.Body:
### Bug `.menu-list` items use a **physical** `text-align: left`, so menu text stays left-aligned under `dir="rtl"` instead of hugging the inline‑start (right) edge. In `sass/components/menu.scss` (Bulma 1.0.4), the `.menu-list a, .menu-list button, .menu-list .menu-item` rule contains: ```scss .menu-list { a, button, .menu-item { // ... display: block; padding: cv.getVar("menu-list-link-padding"); text-align: left; // physical — does not flip under RTL width: 100%; } } ``` Because `text-align: left` is physical rather than logical (`start`), it does not respond to direction. Bulma otherwise adopts logical properties widely and ships no `[dir="rtl"]` overrides, so nothing corrects this at runtime — the menu is the one component that breaks under RTL. ### Reproduce ```html

القائمة

  • لوحة التحكم
  • العناصر
``` `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.menu-list a')).textAlign` is `left`, and the Arabic labels hug the left edge instead of the right. ### Expected Menu items should be inline‑start aligned under RTL. Replacing `text-align: left` with `text-align: start` in that rule fixes it and is consistent with Bulma's use of logical properties elsewhere. ### Environment - Bulma 1.0.4 (compiled `css/bulma.css` and `sass/components/menu.scss`) - Any browser, page or element with `dir="rtl"` (Found while auditing physical vs. logical directional CSS across design systems.)
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "`.menu-list` uses physical `text-align: left`, breaking menu alignment under dir="rtl"" (#4063)

Issues.Title: Spacing scale audit: 37 literal spacing values off your own token scale
Issues.Body:
# Spacing scale audit: 37 literal spacing values off your own token scale

Hi. I maintain [stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard](https://github.com/PetriLahdelma/stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard), a Stylelint rule that checks spacing values against a project's own scale. To keep it quiet on code I do not control, I run it against public design systems on pinned commits and publish the numbers. This repository is one of them, and I would rather you saw the audit here than in a report first.

**What was run.** `npx rhythmguard audit . --scale auto` at `741da22` over `sass`. Hairlines of one pixel or less, percentages, and generated or test paths are excluded. Anyone can reproduce it in a checkout of that commit.

**What it found.** Scale `0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 48` inferred from your own spacing tokens in the stylesheets. 37 literal spacing values are off that scale.

- Values: `2em` ×7, `-0.375em` ×5, `0.375em` ×4, `0.375rem` ×3, `0.1875em` ×2
- Properties: `margin-inline-start` ×6, `margin-bottom` ×5, `margin-inline-end` ×5, `margin-top` ×5, `padding-top` ×4

Three values usually explain most of the count, and each is a single decision: a step the scale is missing, a slip, or a token nobody defined. A property table led by sibling margins often means the parent could own the spacing with `gap`.

**The ask.** Nothing is required. If the numbers are useful, I can open a small PR for the top value with before and after screenshots, or a one-rule Stylelint config at warning level that reports new off-scale values against your tokens and nothing else. If the findings are wrong for this codebase, tell me which ones; false positives are the most valuable report the tool gets and they change its defaults.

The row for this repository will appear in a periodic "State of Spacing" table in the Rhythmguard repository, with this issue linked. If you would rather not be listed, say so here and I will remove it.

Feel free to close this if it is not useful. Thanks for the CSS.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Spacing scale audit: 37 literal spacing values off your own token scale" (#4061)

Issues.Title: fix: hide child elements inside .skeleton-block
Issues.Body:
Fixes #3977

### Problem
Links and other elements with their own text color remain visible inside `.skeleton-block`. The parent's `color: transparent !important` does not cascade to children that have explicit color (e.g. `<a>` elements with browser default `-webkit-link`).

### Fix
Add `* { color: inherit !important; }` inside `.skeleton-block` to force all child elements to inherit the transparent color from the parent.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix: hide child elements inside .skeleton-block" (#4050)

Issues.Title: fix: restore default is-outlined button visibility
Issues.Body:
Fixes #3996

### Problem
Button with class `is-outlined` but without color modifier (like `is-primary`) renders invisible — white text on transparent background. Regression from v0.9.4.

### Root Cause
`$button-l` defaults to `scheme-main-l` (100% = white in light theme). The default filled button does NOT use `button-l` — it uses `button-background-l` for bg, `button-color-l` for text, `button-border-l` for border. But `is-outlined` incorrectly uses `button-l` for BOTH text and border.

### Fix
Change `$button-l` default from `scheme-main-l` to `text-strong-l` (1 character in variable name). Safe because:
- Default filled button doesn't use `button-l`
- Color modifiers override ALL variables
- Loading spinner color also becomes visible
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix: restore default is-outlined button visibility" (#4049)

Issues.Title: fix(menu): use text-align: start so items follow RTL
Issues.Body:
Fixes #4029.

The menu is already mostly migrated to logical properties — the nested list uses `border-inline-start` / `padding-inline-start`. The one physical holdout is item alignment in `sass/components/menu.scss`:

```scss
.menu-list .menu-item,
a,
button { text-align: left; }
```

This forces left alignment regardless of writing direction. Switching to `text-align: start`:

- resolves to `left` in LTR, so it's **identical** there (non-breaking);
- resolves to `right` under `dir="rtl"`, so items align with the writing direction automatically — matching the rest of the component.

Verified on a `.menu` in both directions: items hug the left in LTR and the right in RTL, with nothing else changed.

---

While here, I noticed `.field-label` (`sass/form/tools.scss`) and table `th` (`sass/elements/table.scss`) have the same physical `text-align` — happy to fix those too if you'd like, here or in a follow-up.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(menu): use text-align: start so items follow RTL" (#4048)

Issues.Title: fix(form): correct .control selector edge case for last-child grouping (#4045)
Issues.Body:
This is a bugfix.

Proposed solution

Fix incorrect addon behavior in .control grouping when non-.control siblings (e.g. label) are present. Structural pseudo-classes (:last-child, :only-child, etc.) are replaced with their :of-type equivalents to avoid interference from non-control elements.

Tradeoffs

:of-type is based on element type, not class. Edge cases may still occur if other sibling elements share the same tag name.

Testing Done

Manual test with a label followed by a single .control. Verified correct addon behavior.

Changelog updated?

No.

Issue

Fixes #4045
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(form): correct .control selector edge case for last-child grouping (#4045)" (#4046)

Issues.Title: Documentation web pages not responsive
Issues.Body:
Since the whole point of Bulma is that it consists of responsive CSS, the web pages that document Bulma should be responsive. But they are not.

For example, try to read

https://bulma.io/documentation/start/installation/

on a mobile phone. You can't. The text does not wrap; it runs off the right side of the screen, and you cannot scroll it in order to read it.

I do not know whether this is an issue with the documentation page itself or an underlying flaw in the Bulma-generated CSS. But as a matter of principle it seems to me that the documentation pages should illustrate Bulma in action, in a good way.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Documentation web pages not responsive" (#4041)
